main_text.p:
Constantem inconcussa tamen fiducia mentem
Erigat, atque oculos caelo teneamus apertos,
Docti nusquam humanis confidere rebus.
Nos & nostra videt Deus, aeternumque videbit:
Omnia constanti librata examine pensat
Providus, & recte nil non agit optimus Author.

His Deus exercet nos artibus, hinc nova nobis
Pectora format agens, & casibus urit acerbis
Ne Fidei languens intus fit inutilis ardor,
Neu malesuada pios falsa sub imagine recti
Sopiat in tenebris miserae fiducia pacis.
Sic his saepe suos percellit & implicat olim
Monstris Omnipotens, & nos examine duro
Pertentans, aperit circum mille undique mortes:
Quo sibi nos reddat, quo nos super ardua caeli
Inuitos trahat, atque sui succendat amore,
Doctos nusquam humanis confidere rebus;
Sed Patris arbitrium cupidos vocemque sequentes.
Ista pias adeo formant certamina mentes.

His Deus exercet nos artibus, hinc nova nobis
Pectora fingit agens: adeo nos degener intus
Mens facile immemores caeli, immemoresque bonorum
(Quelis nos Omnipotens ad se trahit & vocat ultro)
Reddiderit, miseros simul ac liquidissima caeli
Tempestas, vultu ridens illuxit amico.

Sed variis ubi turbinibus caelique flagellis
Nos Pater explorans funesta per omnia duxit,
Et doces perferre videt nos aspera quaevis:
Protinus exoluit facilis, laetosque reponit
Securo tutoque loco, damnumque rependit
Munificus Pater, & reficit nos vbere pleno.

Sed tamen interdum totis velut irruat ardens
Irae fulminibus, simulans iam-iam obruit, & iam
Ferri praecipites sub tartara caeca videmur.

page.notes: Transcription is from a slightly faded scan; the handling of the Greek-style ampersand-like sign (&) and of some words in the 16th-century spelling (e.g. "Quelis" in the parenthesis, "Quis" likely) is uncertain and should be checked against the scan. The final word "At" stands alone at the lower right and may be a catchword rather than running text; it is kept in the text here as printed. The running head is "PROTREPTICON". No printed page number is visible. Line-end breaks are marked with line breaks, so verse lines are kept as printed.
